94 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

"Teacher and Teaching" by Hannah Howard; "Writing" by J. D. Warren; "Oratory" by V. M. Tyler.

Mr. G. L. Marshall wrote a lengthy editorial on SAVOY COLLEGE, giving the history of the College and its growth. Other contributors of note in the same issue were J. B. Thompson, N. F. Suddith, W. W. Clem, W. F. Marshall, and others whose names I do not recall.

In November, 1886, taken from the State School Journal is "Into Each Life Some Rain Must Fall." The articles were often in "flowery" language, which provided opportunity for brilliant displays of imagery; but quite frequently this was written in the spirit of the times. About the time he reached the College, a student had had it all a decided lack of awareness, stand out more boldly in the memory. The two which follow are remembered by Mr. Sam W. McKee and related by him.

ADVERTISING—The advertising columns of the paper brought cultural editorial comments in fun. The professors were usually making good use of the paper as a means of financing the college by selling advertising space. News items of note told of frequent visits of the business manager to notify his delinquent subscribers to "Pay Each Life Some Rain Must Fall."
